title: CoMAL: Contrastive Active Learning for Multi-Label Text Classification

problem.claim: Multi-label text classification requires associating texts with multiple labels, but obtaining annotations is expensive and time-consuming.

gap.claim: Existing multi-label active learning still lacks effective ways to represent confusing label semantics and measure a sample's joint effect across the label space.

contributions.claim: CoMAL is a contrastive multi-label active learning framework with a data acquisition strategy.
A contrastive decoupling mechanism releases the semantic information of multiple labels into the latent space.
A hybrid sampling criterion combines similarity-enhanced label cardinality inconsistency with positive feature diversity.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show CoMAL outperforming current state-of-the-art multi-label active learning approaches.
The authors report that code for CoMAL is available on GitHub.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-label text classification supports assigning multiple labels to a text in real-world data mining scenarios.
Annotation is costly, and existing multi-label active learning faces feature-space and sample-selection challenges.
CoMAL addresses the gaps through contrastive decoupling and a hybrid acquisition criterion based on prediction uncertainty and positive semantic diversity.
The authors report that CoMAL outperforms current state-of-the-art multi-label active learning approaches.

source_observation.claim: The method combines uncertainty from label cardinality inconsistency with positive-feature diversity to guide acquisition.

interpretation.claim: Active learning can benefit from jointly modeling prediction uncertainty and semantic diversity under label sparsity.

application.claim: For multi-label annotation workflows, consider acquisition criteria that balance uncertainty with diversity among positively associated labels.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination transfers beyond the evaluated multi-label text classification setting.

unknowns: Datasets, dataset sizes, label counts, and annotation budgets are not specified.
Evaluation metrics, baseline identities, and numerical results are not specified.
The abstract does not describe the implementation details of the contrastive decoupling mechanism or hybrid criterion.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported performance.
